lenses.sp: Wants a large, steady, cheap company with a strong balance sheet.

ch.r: Market value above ₹5,000 crore
ch.w: Graham avoided small companies; ₹5,000 crore is our Indian translation of 'adequate size'.

ch.r: Current assets ÷ current liabilities ≥ 2
ch.w: Doesn't apply: banks and finance companies don't split their balance sheet into current and non-current.

ch.r: Long-term debt ≤ current assets − current liabilities
ch.w: Doesn't apply: borrowing is the raw material of a lender's business.

ch.n: A profit every year for 10 years

ch.v: Profit in all 4 yrs we have
ch.w: No loss in the years we can see; the earlier years are not in the free data.

ch.r: Dividends every year for 20 years (India: 10 years)
ch.w: No dividend on record in the last 10 years.

ch.n: Earnings per share up a third in 10 years
ch.r: EPS +33% over 10 years (3-year averages at each end)
ch.w: EPS (average of the first 2 vs last 2 years we have) moved +75%.

ch.r: PE ≤ 15 on 3-year average earnings
ch.w: You pay ₹16 for every ₹1 of average yearly profit over the last 3 yrs.

ch.r: Price < √(22.5 × EPS × book value per share)

signals.t: Management addressed SMA and ECL questions; no quantified West Asia stress outlook given beyond 'no challenge so far'.
Management would not give a clear view on treasury gains for the next two quarters, citing uncertainty.
Asked about the top-20 borrower concentration, management talked about sector mix and did not give the figures.

Asked about merger news, management said it has no information, verbally or in writing.

Credit cost rose 3 bps quarter on quarter to 0.17%.

Operating income fell 12.89% quarter on quarter while net profit rose, driven by a large swing in non-interest income.
Miscellaneous fee income dropped 93.81% year on year in the quarter after a large Jun-26 figure.
Q-o-Q net profit and operating profit growth slowed sharply versus the 49% year-on-year jump; domestic CASA ratio slipped slightly q-o-q.
Recovery from technical written-off accounts and some earlier income lines fell sharply in the quarter.

story.what_it_does: IOB (Indian Overseas Bank) takes deposits and makes loans, with retail, agriculture and MSME (the 'RAM' segments) making up about 79% of domestic advances. At March 2026 domestic deposits were Rs.3,59,032 crore and domestic gross advances were Rs.2,94,405 crore. It also runs overseas and treasury operations.
story.plans: Management guided for NIM of about 3.3% to 3.4% and full-year FY27 credit cost of 0.35% to 0.40%. It also talked about raising Rs.5,000 crore of equity in Q3 or Q4, front-loading the roughly Rs.3,000 crore expected-credit-loss (ECL) need, and adding 1,069 cash recyclers in FY27. Other stated targets include Rs.3,600 crore of recoveries this year and FCNR deposit and GIFT City growth.
story.moat: The notes do not describe a clear competitive edge. What they show is a large branch network (1,073 branches covered by branch auditors) and a CASA (low-cost deposit) share of about 41%, which has been drifting down. Management itself gave no concrete valuation or franchise milestones.

scenarios.story: Profit keeps growing, with Q2 FY27 net profit at Rs.1,912 crore (up 55.95%), while gross NPA falls to 1.19% and loans grow 24.35%. Capital stays well above minimums at 18.60% and margins hold in the guided range.
signals_to_watch: Gross NPA ratio staying below 1.19% and net NPA staying at or below 0.16%
Net interest margin holding in the 3.3% to 3.4% guided range

scenarios.story: Loans and deposits keep growing at a double-digit pace, while credit cost moves toward the 0.35% to 0.40% full-year guide as ECL provisioning is front-loaded. Profit growth slows from recent highs as one-off income fades.
signals_to_watch: Credit cost against the 0.35% to 0.40% full-year guidance (0.17% in Q2 FY27)
Recoveries against the Rs.3,600 crore target for this year

scenarios.story: CASA share keeps slipping and capital falls (CRAR dropped to 18.60%) as fast loan growth lifts risk-weighted assets. Profit leans on lumpy items such as the Rs.921 crore miscellaneous income in Jun-26, treasury gains and recoveries, which management would not quantify, and overseas bad loans stay high.
signals_to_watch: CRAR and CASA ratio quarter-on-quarter (CRAR down 76 bps and CASA lower in Q2 FY27)
Overseas gross NPA ratio (8.79% at March 2026) and non-interest income swings
